note: Single source of truth for what each paid plan actually allows. Read by server-billing.cjs (enforcement) and src/content/pricing.ts (the pricing page and comparison table), so an advertised limit and an enforced limit cannot drift apart. Every limit here MUST have a server-side check — if you add one with no enforcement, you are selling something you do not deliver. null means unlimited.

enforcement.facilities: server.cjs POST /api/companies/:id/facilities, counted under a company-row lock (server-entry-routes.cjs insertFacilityWithinCap)
enforcement.csvImportsPerMonth: server.cjs POST /api/ingest/csv (server-csv-import-routes.cjs), counted from public.csv_import_events under a company-row lock: one per committed import; dry runs, refused files, duplicates and replayed requests spend nothing; an undone import still counts
enforcement.scope3: server.cjs POST /api/calculate, POST /api/ingest/csv, POST /api/entries and PATCH /api/entries/:id
enforcement.activePlan: server.cjs requirePlan on every data route, including GET/POST /api/entries and PATCH /api/entries/:id (DELETE /api/entries/:id stays open after the trial, like the export)
enforcement.directWrites: Until docs/deferred-migrations/20260930130000_revoke-authenticated-writes.sql is applied, the records API still accepts direct emission_entries/facilities writes from the browser role: the limits above bind the app, not a hand-made records API call
